assignment.title: Soft Touch to Speed
assignment.note: Soft touches, quick feet—speed up only while the ball stays close.

drills.title: Toe Taps
drills.instructions:
Setup: Place the ball on the ground in front of you in a clear space.
Alternate light toe taps on the ball, switching feet each touch. Start slowly and build the rhythm only while you stay balanced and in control.
Focus: Keep the taps soft and your balance steady.

drills.title: Inside–Outside Cone Touches
drills.instructions:
Setup: Set four cones in a straight line about a yard apart, with room to turn at the end.
Use the inside and outside of the active foot to dribble down the line and back. Keep that same foot for the whole interval; the next interval uses the other foot. Start slowly and speed up only while the ball stays close.
Focus: Use small inside and outside touches to guide the ball around each cone.

drills.title: Close-Control Cone Circuit
drills.instructions:
Setup: Set four cones in a small square and a fifth in the middle. Leave enough room to turn comfortably between them.
Dribble around the middle and outside cones, using both feet. Change direction and repeat. Begin slowly, then build speed only while each touch stays within easy reach.
Focus: Soft, close touches. Stay in control through each turn.

assignment.title: Agility foundations
assignment.note: Warm up for 4 minutes, then complete each exercise in order. Allow about 15–20 minutes including rests and an easy 2-minute finish. Springy contacts, trunk control and leg endurance support your agility work. Stop any exercise that causes pain.

drills.title: Glute bridges
drills.instructions:
Setup: Use a mat on a firm floor. Before the session, warm up for 4 minutes with easy marching or jogging, ankle circles and comfortable bodyweight squats. Lie on your back, bend your knees and place both feet flat about hip-width apart.
Press through your feet and raise your hips by squeezing your glutes. Pause for 2 seconds, then lower slowly. Keep your ribs settled rather than lifting higher by arching your back. One lift and lower is one rep. Finish both sets before moving on.
Focus: Smooth, even hip lift. Leave a few good repetitions in reserve.

drills.title: Pogos
drills.instructions:
Setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart on a level, non-slip surface with clear space overhead. Complete the warm-up before jumping.
Make small two-foot hops, using a quick ankle spring and a soft knee bend. Land quietly in the same spot and keep the hops low. Count each landing as one rep. Pause and reset if the rhythm or landing control fades; do not chase height. Rest the full minute between sets.
Focus: Light, quiet contacts. If hopping is uncomfortable, stop the set and use controlled calf raises instead.

drills.title: Mountain climbers
drills.instructions:
Setup: Use a firm, non-slip floor or mat. Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders.
Bring one knee towards your chest, return that foot, then alternate legs. Begin with deliberate steps and build a steady rhythm only while your hips stay level. Keep breathing and avoid bouncing through your lower back. Work for 20 seconds, then rest for 40 seconds.
Focus: Stable shoulders and trunk. Slow the steps if you start rocking.

drills.title: Wall sits
drills.instructions:
Setup: Use a solid wall and a non-slip floor. Place your back against the wall and walk your feet forward, about hip-width apart.
Slide into a comfortable squat depth and hold with both feet flat and knees following your toes. A shallower position is fine; do not force a right angle. Keep breathing normally. Hold for up to 30 seconds, then stand and rest for 45 seconds before the next set.
Focus: Steady position without breath-holding. After the final set, walk easily for 2 minutes.
